articleTitle: Medium speed access to local area atm
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This article proposes an access mechanism to asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) networks by which ATM type services can be cost effectively provided to lower performance workstations. A distributed ATM switch, based on a slotted ring architecture, is used. The proposed design of the host adapter card also enables a smooth upgrade path to centralised ATM switches.

articleTitle: Software which automatically routes cables in a power reticulation design system
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The subject of this paper is the development of an automatic cable router for use in the design of electricity distribution networks. Very little previous research has been done on finding optimal cable routing configurations from first principles. By “first principles”, we mean that the problem is approached by considering a set of points as input and not an enumeration of all possible paths (from which an optimal solution is obtained by search). The research described in this paper approaches the problem from first principles leading to the development of two prototypes. The Lee router is based on a printed circuit board routing method and the Track router is based on computational geometry. Both prototypes will find the optimal routes between a set of points while avoiding predefined obstacles. The set of points represents substations, junctions and consumer connections, while the obstacles represent areas that the distribution cables may not cross.

articleTitle: An explicit design criterion for the RF choke reactance on the class E power amplifiers and frequency multipliers
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The theoretical performances of the class E amplifier/multiplier with RF choke have been previously obtained under the assumption of an infinite inductance of the RF choke. This paper examines the influence of the RF choke inductance on the class E amplifier/multiplier, giving an explicit design criterion for the RF choke inductance.

articleTitle: A coherent procedure for dynamic stabilisation using power system stabilisers
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents a technique for technique for power system stabilisation using Power System Stabilisers (PSS). The method encompasses the main problems associated with the use of PSS. Three problems are addressed, namely the optimal locations of the PSS, the most effective signal for stabilisation and the determination of values of the PSS parameters. Novel concepts such as exciter penalty factors, modified coupling factors and power system decentralised fixed modes are presented. The method is implemented on a benchmark network and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Leakage current monitoring on synthetic insulators at a severe coastal site
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In order to evaluate the effect of coastal pollution on power line insulators, an insulator test station was established at Elandsbaai on the west coast of South Africa, 250 km from Cape Town. The station is in a winter rainfall area with build-up of pollution during the dry summer months. The 30 minute highest leakage currents are stored on a continuous basis together with weather data using a dedicated microprocessor based data logger. Twelve insulators of different designs, materials and specific creepage lengths (including silicone rubber and EPDM), are used as test samples. The station is energised from a 50 kV traction line, via explosive fuses. The design and operational history of the station is discussed. Despite certain operational problems, results for a period of more than 3 years are presented and interpreted together with the relevant weather data. The insulator surface is inspected regularly. The importance of hydrophobicity and the effects of humidity and natural rain washing are confirmed. The eventual aim is to relate maximum leakage current to specific creepage and insulator shed material.

articleTitle: Real world interfacing with transputers
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The transputer is a high performance microprocessor with an instruction throughput of 10 MIPS supporting parallel processing. The question arise as to how to get data into and from a transputer or transputer network. This paper focus on the mechanisms available on the transputer and evaluate them according to Software complexity, Hardware complexity and maximum attainable data bandwidth. Where possible examples are included of implementations at Stellenbosch University. Novel direct memory access mechanisms are proposed which becomes viable only due to the performance of the microprocessor itself.

articleTitle: The partial series resonant converter: A new zero voltage switching DC to DC converter
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A variation of the series resonant converter is proposed which clamps the capacitor voltage, and effectively inhibits the resonance for a part of the cycle. The resonant capacitors are charged to the supply voltage during each half cycle and discharged into the load. Output power is controlled by adjusting the rate of pulsed energy transfer to the load. This circuit behaves differently than the conventional series resonant converter, and advantages include operation below rather than above resonance making it possible to attain a high frequency power product using slower semiconductor switches. The circuit can be operated as either a zero current switching or a zero voltage switching converter. Zero voltage switching is the preferred mode of operation and includes the addition of a parallel inductor. Experimental results are presented on a 6kW battery charger, using IGBT's and switching at 50kHz.

articleTitle: A condition for asymptotic setpoint tracking in internal model control loops
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Asymptotic tracking of setpoints in Internal Model Control (IMC) structures is ensured by imposing a set of criteria based on derivatives of the transfer function [1-q(s)g(s)] when designing the IMC module q(s). Simpler algebraic constraints on the numerator polynomial of q(s) that give a particular Type Number for the final IMC system are developed here. An application to the design of feedback controllers for a servo motor demonstrates that the proposed algebraic constraints produce asymptotic setpoint tracking, and that the IMC performance is not sensitive to modelling accuracy.

articleTitle: Aspects and improvements in rolling rotor switched reluctance motors
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents an explanation on the method of torque production of the rolling rotor motor. Making use of an internal electromechanical speed reduction mechanism this motor is able to produce a high direct torque without the use of a gearbox. The rotor is free to roll around the inside of the stator without bearings restraining it to a fixed axis. Attention is drawn to the robustness and simplicity of the motor, making it ideal for low cost applications, where a large torque at low speeds is required from a compact gearless construction. A finite element analysis was also performed on the motor which gave valuable design considerations.

articleTitle: Control methods for the nonlinear resonant pole inverter
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A new version of the resonant pole inverter includes a saturating inductor and a current feedback winding. The standard resonant pole inverter becomes a special case of this inverter and design degrees of freedom increase significantly. In this paper the focus is on the control of this new type of inverter, and switching frequency variation and dynamic response is addressed. It is shown that a saturating inductor can improve the stability of the switching frequency while very fast dynamic response is possible in case of an inductive load. Experimental results are also presented.

articleTitle: Telecommunication networks and services for rural application in Africa
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper investigates the telecommunication networks and services which countries in Africa can assimilate in order to disseminate information to the rural population. The most efficient and cost effective networks are those using flexible radio links and in this paper they are given more emphasis. In this survey terrestrial radio systems including point-to-point, point-to-multipoint and multiaccess technologies are investigated. The use of mobile communication techniques and equipment for fixed services is considered and the network options offered by satellite links are also presented. Such networks can provide the traditional services of telephony, telegraphy, telex and data dissemination but due to the unique educational needs of the rural population audio-visual services, using the same networks are recommended for spreading news and information for tele-education, entertainment and advertising.

articleTitle: Implementation strategy for a fail-silent processing node for distributed computer control
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A difficulty in constructing dependable, fault-tolerant distributed computer control systems is the problem of preventing faults in one part the system from spreading to other parts. A theoretical solution is to design system components so that when they fail it is ensured that they produce no output. Techniques such as graceful degradation, standby redundancy and active redundancy can then be used at the system level to compensate for such failed components. The implementation strategy used in an experimental prototype fail-silent processing node intended for use in real-time distributed computer control systems is discussed and issues that arise are analysed.

articleTitle: A fuzzy logic approach to direct phase-controlled converter DC machine drive
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An application of fuzzy logic in controlling the speed of a dc machine drive (DCM) is proposed. The control system relies on cascaded speed and voltage control loops. The inner fuzzy logic phase-locked loop for voltage control operates without detecting the line voltage. The outer speed control loop is based on a fuzzy logic controller. A rule-based algorithm speeds the start-up performance. Simulation of the entire system is performed on computer and the results show good dynamic and steady-state behaviors.

articleTitle: A study of the effectivity of reducing the energy storage element in dynamic filters for compensation of non-active power
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The instantaneous power theory was used to obtain the different load power components. The possibility of compensating for detrimental power components by means of different compensating modes, using hybrid power electronic active filters were investigated in order to obtain the most economical compensator topology.

articleTitle: Approximate computer modelling of a Manpack antenna using the two dimensional finite element/boundary element method
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A two dimensional Finite Element/Boundary Element (FE/BE) method for solving electromagnetic scattering from human cross-sections has been investigated, implemented, validated and used to investigate — approximately — the electromagnetic interaction of a manpack radio with its operator. Validation has been done by comparing results computed using analytical solutions for scattering from multi-layered right circular dielectric cylinders with line source excitation. The problem of a manpack antenna, which by definition radiates in the very close presence of the operator, has been approximated by a two dimensional model of a representative human cross-section with a line source radiating cylindrical waves modelling the antenna. From the FE/BE method solution one can obtain approximations of the near fields in and around the human cross-section, as well as the far-fields. This enables one to calculate the power dissipated in the human cross-section (the effect of the radio on the operator) as well as the influence of the human cross-section on the far-field pattern of the line source (i.e., the effect of the operator on the radio). We comment on possible applications to radiation hazard evaluation for personnel, and also outline further work required in this field.

articleTitle: Comparison between hard switched and resonant pole inverters based on component losses
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Zero voltage switching in resonant inverters has proven itself as an effective way to minimize the switching losses present in high frequency inverters. The resonant pole inverter has lately been identified as a suitable inverter for larger power levels. Switching times are not directly related to switching losses as in the case for hard switching - a fact which can be used to advantage when selecting devices. On the other hand, larger than 1 p.u. peak device current stresses are present which requires overdimensioning of the switches and could give rise to larger conduction losses in the semiconductor devices. The resonant pole inverter requires an additional inductor which further contributes to losses. In this paper the losses are modelled and the trade-off between the different loss components and suitability of device types are investigated using the hard switched inverter as reference. An important conclusion is that semiconductor power devices need to be designed differently for soft switching application, with more emphasis on reduction of conduction losses.

articleTitle: The influence of phase shifts between parallel generators on SSR studies near incipient stability
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The phase relationships between the torsional oscillations of parallel generators is studied in the region of incipient stability of the torsional modes of that system. The generators are considered to be identical apart from differences in their individual mechanical dampings. The results confirm that a difference in mechanical dampings of the two machines results in phase deviations between their torsional oscillations, but show that these deviations are not negligible near incipient stability. These phase shifts near incipient stability may affect estimates made of the combined mechanical damping of the system for certain torsional modes.
